title_as_printed: Region-specific Cerebral Metabolic Alterations in Parkinson’s Disease Patients With/without Mild Cognitive Impairment

blind_codes.Sample_N: 63 (25 HC + 18 PDN + 20 PDMCI); 57 completed PFC scans

Task_Type.reason: Besides ANCOVA group comparisons and correlations, the paper evaluates metabolite cut-points by ROC (AUC, sensitivity, specificity, cut-off) for PDMCI vs HC and PDMCI vs PDN, which is a stated aim. Discrimination is quantified, so T1 under the deciding test.
Task_Type.quote: The combination of thalamic and PCC metabolites showed a 75.6% accuracy in distinguishing PDMCI patients from PDN patients.

Category.reason: Single-voxel 1H-MRS on a 3T MRI scanner (in vivo neuroimaging).

Validation_Type.reason: ROC cut-points derived and evaluated on the whole sample; no cross-validation or test set, so V2.

Sample_N_Approx.reason: 25 HC + 18 PDN + 20 PDMCI = 63 (57 completed the PFC scan).
Sample_N_Approx.quote: A total of 63 subjects were recruited, of which 57 of them finished the last scans in ROI of PFC regions.

notes: The MCI here is Parkinson's-disease MCI (PD-MCI), and the main discrimination reported is PDMCI vs cognitively normal PD; this matters if the census pools T1 discrimination figures as AD-continuum MCI vs HC.
